seo.title: How to Link Google Ads to Google Analytics
seo.meta_description: How to link Google Ads to Google Analytics 4, what permissions you need and why it helps Anaheim and Orange County advertisers measure leads, not just clicks.

h1: How to Link Google Ads to Google Analytics 4
answer: To link Google Ads to Google Analytics, go to Admin, Product links, Google Ads links in your GA4 property, click Link and choose your Google Ads account. You need Editor or Administrator access in Analytics and administrative access in Google Ads. Linking lets Anaheim and Orange County advertisers see what ad clicks lead to and create conversions from key events.
key_takeaways: Link from Admin, Product links, Google Ads links.
Needs Editor or Admin in GA4 and admin access in Ads.
Create conversions from your key events.

sections.heading: Why link the two
sections.body_html: Google's help page says linking lets you see the full customer cycle, from how people interact with your ads to whether they complete key events on your site. With a link, you can create consistent conversions based on key events, view Google Ads conversion performance and re-engage visitors based on their behavior.

sections.heading: What Google reports about linking
sections.body_html: Google states that customers who link Google Ads or Google Marketing Platform accounts to an Analytics property are correlated with a 23% increase in conversions and a 10% reduction in cost per conversion. That is a correlation Google reports, not a guarantee for your account.

sections.heading: Permissions you need
sections.body_html: Google says you must be an administrator or editor of the Analytics property, and the Google account needs administrative access in Google Ads. If you link a manager account, data imported from Analytics is available to all its client accounts.

sections.heading: How to link
sections.body_html:
1. In GA4 Admin, under Product links, click Google Ads links.
  2. Click Link.
  3. Click Choose Google Ads accounts and select the accounts.
  4. If you lack access, use Request access to other Google Ads accounts.
  5. Review the settings and submit.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body_html: Google says you can create up to 400 links per property, and a link to a manager account counts as one link. Most small businesses need only one.

sections.heading: Auto-tagging
sections.body_html: When Google Ads is linked, auto-tagging passes campaign details to Analytics, so you don't need UTM parameters on those ads. Ad clicks then appear correctly in Traffic acquisition.

sections.heading: Use key events as conversions
sections.body_html: Once linked, you can create Google Ads conversions from your Analytics key events, such as quote requests, so bidding optimizes toward real leads.

sections.heading: Check the link works
sections.body_html: After linking, check that Google Ads traffic appears as paid search in Traffic acquisition, and that conversions imported from key events show in Google Ads after some activity.

sections.heading: Remember invalid traffic
sections.body_html: Google filters invalid clicks from ad billing. Compare ad-driven key events with real leads in your records to judge quality, not just volume.

sections.heading: Common mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Linking with an account that lacks admin access in Ads.
  • Importing both a key event and a duplicate Ads conversion for the same action.
  • Turning off auto-tagging.
  • Judging ads by sessions instead of key events.
  • Linking the wrong Ads account.

sections.heading: What to review after linking
sections.body_html: A month after linking, compare three numbers for your paid campaigns: clicks in Google Ads, sessions from paid search in Analytics and key events from those sessions. Clicks and sessions won't match exactly, because a click doesn't always load a page and sessions are counted differently, but a large gap can point to slow landing pages or tracking problems. Then look at which campaigns and keywords bring key events, not just visits, and move budget toward them. For Orange County service businesses, it's common to find that a few specific searches, such as emergency repair or a specific city and service, bring most leads, while broad terms bring browsers. Linking the two products is what makes that visible.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Editor or admin access in GA4.
  • Admin access in Google Ads.
  • Link created.
  • Auto-tagging on.
  • Conversions from key events set.
  • Paid traffic visible in reports.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine an HVAC company in Orange that runs Google Ads but measures only clicks. After linking Ads to Analytics and importing its quote-request key event as a conversion, it sees that emergency AC repair searches bring most quote requests, while general HVAC searches bring visits but few leads. It shifts budget accordingly.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: It helps to see where this sits in the bigger picture. Google ranks local results mainly on relevance, distance and popularity, and AI assistants lean on the same public information: your Business Profile, your website, other listings and what customers write. For a business in Anaheim or anywhere in Orange County, the most reliable plan is simple and repeated: keep every listing accurate, explain each service clearly on its own page, show real proof of your work and reply to customers. Small improvements here compound, and they are far harder for competitors to copy than an ad budget.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Check your access in both products.
  2. Create the link in GA4 Admin.
  3. Import key events as conversions.
  4. Review leads by campaign next month.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Plenty of owners handle this themselves. Outside help pays off when time is short, when the business has many locations or when a problem is costing calls every day it stays unresolved. Be wary of anyone who promises guaranteed positions or asks for your verification codes or passwords; Google says nobody can pay for a better local ranking. Look for clear explanations, honest timelines and reporting tied to real enquiries. Chimera offers exactly that to businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether linking shares their data with Google in new ways. Linking allows data to flow between your own Analytics property and Ads account for the purposes Google describes, such as conversions and audiences; review the link settings and your privacy policy to make sure they match how you use the data. Another common question is whether to import key events or use the Google Ads tag for conversions. Importing key events keeps both products consistent and is simpler for most small businesses, as long as you don't count the same action twice. Owners also ask whether a link helps Local Services Ads. It doesn't; Local Services Ads have their own lead reporting. Finally, owners ask how long until bidding improves. Smart bidding needs a steady flow of conversions, so give it several weeks before judging the change. Keep notes of any bidding or budget changes so you can match them to results later, and review lead quality alongside the conversion count.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Link Google Ads from GA4 Admin, keep auto-tagging on and create conversions from key events, then judge campaigns by leads. Chimera, based in Anaheim, links and audits Ads and Analytics for Orange County businesses.
